meta.title: We never charge candidates
meta.description: Venkat Sai Global never charges candidates for a job. Learn how recruitment fraud works, the warning signs, how to verify an Indian recruiting agent on eMigrate and how to report a suspicious offer.
hero.title: Venkat Sai Global never charges candidates
hero.description: You never pay us to find a job, apply, be shortlisted, be interviewed or take a trade test for a role. Employers pay for our recruitment services. If anyone asks you for money for a job in our name, it is not us.

promise.title: Our promise to candidates
promise.free: Searching and applying for jobs on Venkat Sai Global is free.
promise.noTestFee: A trade test or assessment linked to a job is paid for by the employer or by Venkat Sai, never by you.
promise.noCourseCondition: Training is optional. Paying for a course is never a condition for an application, an offer or a placement.
promise.official: We contact you only through your account on this website, and by email or phone from our official contact details listed on our contact page.
promise.domain: Our official website address is {domain}. Treat links to look-alike addresses as suspicious.
how.title: How recruitment fraud usually works
how.intro: Fraudsters copy the names and logos of real companies and agencies. The pattern is often the same:
how.step1: An attractive offer arrives on WhatsApp, social media or by phone, often for a job abroad with a high salary.
how.step2: There is little or no interview, and you are told you have been selected quickly.
how.step3: You are asked to pay for registration, a visa, a medical, a ticket or "processing", usually to a personal bank account or UPI ID.
how.step4: After you pay, more fees appear, or the contact stops replying. Some people travel on a visit visa and find there is no job.
signs.title: Warning signs
signs.fee: You are asked to pay a fee to get a job, an interview, a visa or an offer letter.
signs.email: Messages come from free email addresses (such as Gmail or Yahoo) or unofficial domains instead of the company's own.
signs.pressure: You are pressured to pay quickly, "today only", or told that seats are running out.
signs.noInterview: You are offered a job without a proper interview or skills check.
signs.passport: Someone asks you to hand over your original passport or documents before any written offer.
signs.visitVisa: You are told to travel on a tourist or visit visa and "convert it" to a work visa later.
signs.noContract: There is no written employment contract, or the contract differs from what you were promised.
signs.unregistered: The agent cannot show a recruiting agent registration certificate, or it does not appear on the eMigrate portal.
verify.title: How to verify an Indian recruiting agent
verify.intro: Recruiting agents in India who send workers abroad must be registered with the Protector General of Emigrants under the Emigration Act, 1983. You can check an agent yourself on the Government of India's eMigrate portal.
verify.step1: Ask the agent for their recruiting agent registration certificate number.
verify.step2: Open the official eMigrate portal and look up the list of registered recruiting agents.
verify.step3: Search for the agent by name or registration number and check that the name, address and validity match what you were told.
verify.step4: If the agent is not listed, the registration has expired, or the details do not match, do not pay and do not hand over documents.
verify.jobs: On our job board, overseas jobs advertised by or for a recruiting agent show the agent's name and eMigrate registration number once our team has recorded it, so you can check them.
help.title: Help from the Government of India
help.pbsk: The Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra is the Ministry of External Affairs helpline for Indians working or planning to work abroad. Its current contact numbers are listed on the official Ministry of External Affairs and eMigrate websites.
help.madad: Indians abroad can raise consular grievances through the Ministry of External Affairs' MADAD portal.
help.cyber: If you have lost money to a fraudster, report it to the police and on the national cyber crime reporting portal.
help.external: (official website, opens in a new tab)
report.title: Report a suspicious offer to us
report.body: If someone asked you for money for a job in the name of Venkat Sai Global, or you are unsure whether an offer is genuine, tell us. Do not pay anything while we check.
report.keep: Keep the evidence: messages, phone numbers, payment requests and any documents you were sent.
report.how: Use the grievance form and choose "General grievance". You will get a reference number and our response timelines.
report.cta: Report it through the grievance form
disclaimer: This page is general guidance, not legal advice. Always check details on the official government websites linked above.
